description: Maintainer-reviewed finite selection of official runnable robotics examples. Every project and artifact is immutable; this is not an exhaustive internet inventory. Source code is referenced, not redistributed or executed.
refresh_policy: Change the commit only after upstream and license review, then run explicit --discover, review the diff, and run --fetch --check. Normal builds are offline; no automatic code execution.

projects.name: PythonRobotics

license.scope: Selected PythonRobotics algorithm demonstration source under the pinned MIT license text, Copyright (c) 2016 - now Atsushi Sakai and other contributors. Preserve repository license and each selected file's author notices. This is source-text scope only; dependencies, mathematical references, generated plots and any external assets retain separate terms. GitHub's automated classifier reports NOASSERTION; the MIT identity here comes from the exact reviewed LICENSE bytes, not that classifier.

requirements.python: Upstream README and requirements/environment.yml declare Python 3.13.x; no interpreter/package combination was installed or tested.
packages: matplotlib==3.11.2 (repository requirements declaration; all five scripts import pyplot)
numpy==2.5.3 (repository requirements declaration; four selected entrypoints import numpy)
scipy==1.18.1 (repository requirements declaration; Hybrid A* imports scipy.spatial)
cvxpy==1.9.3 (repository requirements declaration; selected MPC source only, which calls solver=cvxpy.CLARABEL)
ecos==2.0.14 (repository requirements declaration; not substituted for the selected MPC source's CLARABEL solver)
Matching pinned in-repository helpers for Hybrid A* and MPC; this individual source-file reference is not a full runnable bundle
requirements.environment: Mathematical planning/tracking demonstrations with hard-coded maps, goals and simulated dynamics; no hardware controller or exact robot model is identified. Matplotlib animation is enabled in source and requires suitable display/backend configuration. A*/D* Lite/DWA imports are stdlib/Matplotlib/NumPy; Hybrid A* also imports local dynamic_programming_heuristic, car, ReedsSheppPath.reeds_shepp_path_planning and SciPy; MPC imports utils.angle, PathPlanning.CubicSpline.cubic_spline_planner and cvxpy/CLARABEL. Use the exact upstream checkout/layout and read its setup. Dependency versions and optional GUI/solver support are declarations, not verified runtime compatibility.

projects.invocation_notes: Run the selected Python main only after independent upstream dependency, GUI/backend and local-helper setup review. These are numerical algorithm demonstrations, not commands for physical robots or ready deployment policies. The repository recommends pip requirements/requirements.txt or conda requirements/environment.yml; those are upstream declarations and were not executed. Keep the exact checkout layout for local imports. Five sources were only read, hashed and parsed; no Hub adapter, installation, simulation result, robot-model support or compatible runtime combination is asserted.
